pages.text: 190-10 July 20, 2010 RESOLUTION TO INCREAS E PUBLIC BIDDING THRESHOLD WHEREAS, the Public Bidding Threshold for Public Units is adjusted every five years by the State Governor in consultation with the Department of Treasury; and WHEREAS, the Township of West Orange desires to take advantage of the increased bid threshold enabling the award the reoccurring goods and services more expeditiously; and WHEREAS, pursuant to the provisions of the Local Public Contracts Law N.J.S.A. 40A:11-3c Public Law as authorized by the New Jersey State Treasurer, The Township of West Orange can increase it’s Public Bidding Threshold from $29, 000.00 to $36,000.00 if the Township has a Qualified Purchasing Agent; and WHEREAS, through resolution, Anne DeSantis is designated a Qualified Purchasing Agent as issued by the Director of the Division of Local Government Services in accordance with N.J.A.C. 5:34-5 et seq. and N.J.S.A. 40A:11-3. NOW, THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED, that the Council of the Township of West Orange, in the County of Essex, in the State of New Jersey hereby increases its Public Bidding Threshold to $36,000.00. Karen J. Carnevale, Municipal Clerk Sal M. Anderton, Council President Adopted: July 20, 2010

154-10 June 15, 2010 RESOLUTION WHEREAS, certain ABC charges have been brought against Duran & Vera, t/a El Rancho, Licensee # 0722-33-039-006/007, and are scheduled to be heard by the Township of West Orange ABC Board on the evening of June 15, 2010; and WHEREAS, some potential witnesses expected to participate in the hearing speak and/or understand only Spanish; and WHEREAS, a Spanish/English interpreter is needed to assist the witnesses, counsel and the ABC Board to provide and understand the testimony of at least some of the anticipated witnesses and to ensure that the requirements of due process of law are met; and WHEREAS, Maria Voltmer is a court certified Spanish/English interpreter, doing business as Maria’s Interpreting Service, located in the Township of West Orange; and WHEREAS, Maria Voltmer is willing and able to provide her interpreting services to the ABC Board for its hearing of the ABC charges against El Rancho at the rate of $60 per hour with a three (3) hour minimum; NOW, THEREFORE, IT IS AND HEREBY IS, RESOLVED by the Township Council of the Township of West Orange, that the Mayor shall be authorized to execute a contract for the provision of interpreter services by Maria Voltmer, Maria’s Interpreting Service, West Orange, NJ, at the rate of $60 per hour with a three (3) hour minimum, for acting as a Spanish/English interpreter at the ABC Board hearing on charges of ABC violations now pending against Duran & Vera, t/a El Rancho, Licensee # 0722-33-039-006/007, scheduled to be heard on the evening of June 15, 2010. _________________________________ ____________________________________ Karen J. Carnevale Susan McCartney
Municipal Clerk Council President Adopted: June 15, 2010

153-10 June 15, 2010 R E S O L U T I O N WHEREAS, the Township of West Orange desires to make infrastructure improvements known as the Mayfair District Storm and Sanitary Sewer Improvements to alleviate flooding on Nestro Road, Midro Way, Mayfair Drive, Rosemont Terrace and Rosemont Drive; and WHEREAS, the Township will require easements from various property owners within the district to construct the improvements; and WHEREAS, the Township Engineer has negotiated Deeds of Easement and Easement Agreements with twelve property owners in the district which represents just under one half of the total easements required; and WHEREAS, a list of the Grantors (property owners) property address, property identifiers and the consideration for the easements along with a copy of the Easement Agreements are attached hereto and made a part hereof; and WHEREAS, the Township Engineer recommends the Township accept these Agreements and authorize the Mayor to execute them; and WHEREAS, the Township Council concurs in the foregoing. NOW THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED by the Township of West Orange that the Mayor is authorized to execute the attached Easement Agreements and the Township Clerk shall attest his signature. Karen J. Carnevale Susan McCartney Township Clerk Council President Adopted: June 15, 2010 Approved as to form on the basis of the facts provided:

54-10 February 23, 2010 RESOLUTION WHEREAS, Sunrise West Orange NJ Senior Living, LLC (“Sunrise”), a Delaware limited liability company, owns certain real property and any improvements located thereon located at 577 Mount Pleasant Avenue in West Orange, New Jersey (the “Property”); and WHEREAS, Sunrise desires to sell the Property; and WHEREAS, the Township of West Orange (the “Township”) desires to purchase the Property subject to certain terms and conditions set forth in the annexed Purchase and Sale Agreement (the “Agreement”); and WHEREAS, the Township is in the process of submitting all appropriate applications and documentation to the State of New Jersey Department of Environmental Protection Green Acres Program (“Green Acres”) for funding a portion of the cost to acquire the property; and WHEREAS, the Township has negotiated in good faith with Sunrise and reached an agreement to purchase the Property for $1,120,000; a nd WHEREAS, the Township Attorney has negotiated the annexed Agreement; and WHEREAS, the Chief Financial Officer of the Township has certified as to the availability of funds fo r the agreement; NOW, BE IT HEREBY RESOLVED BY THE TOWNSHIP COUNCIL OF THE TOWNSHIP OF WEST ORANGE that the Mayor be and hereby is authorized to execute a copy of the Agreement of Sale annexed hereto and the Municipal Clerk be and is hereby authorized to attest to the Mayor’s signature; and it further RESOLVED that the Mayor, Director of Planning and Development, Chief Financial Officer, Business Administrator, Municipal Engineer and Township Attorney be and hereby are authorized to take all steps reasonably necessary to finalize the acquisition of the Property. Karen J. Carnevale Honorable Susan McCartney Township Clerk Council President Adopted: February 23,2010 Approved as to form on the basis of the facts provided: Richard D. Trenk Township Attorney

documents.title: OF THE TOW NSHIP OF WEST ORANGE, COUNTY OF ESSEX, NEW JERSEY REFERRING PROPOSED THIRD AMENDMENT TO THE DOWNTOWN REDEVELOPMENT PLAN TO THE TOWNSHIP PLANNING BOARD FOR ITS REVIEW AND COMMENT PURSUANT TO THE LOCAL REDEVELOPMENT AND HOUSING LAW

pages.text: 343-10 December 14, 2010 RESOLUTION OF THE TOW NSHIP OF WEST ORANGE, COUNTY OF ESSEX, NEW JERSEY REFERRING PROPOSED THIRD AMENDMENT TO THE DOWNTOWN REDEVELOPMENT PLAN TO THE TOWNSHIP PLANNING BOARD FOR ITS REVIEW AND COMMENT PURSUANT TO THE LOCAL REDEVELOPMENT AND HOUSING LAW WHEREAS, the Township Council of the Township of West Orange (the “Township Council”) heretofore duly adopted a Resolution determining that an area within the West Orange downtown area (the “Downtown Redevelopment Area”) was an “area in need of redevelopment” in accordance with N.J.S.A. 40A:12A-6(b); and WHEREAS, in accordance with the provisions of N.J.S.A. 40A:12A-7 the Township Council on February 9, 2003 approved an ordinance adopting a redevelopment plan for the Downtown Redevelopment Area (the “ Initial Redevelopment Plan”); and WHEREAS, on August 15, 2006, the Township Council approved an ordinance adopting certain amendments (the “ First Amendment”) to the Initial Redevelopment Plan (as so amended, the “First Amended Redevelopment Plan”); and WHEREAS, on March 6, 2007, the Township Council approved an ordinance adopting certain further amendments (the “Second Amendment”) to the First Amended Redevelopment Plan (as so amended, the “Redevelopment Plan”); and WHEREAS, the Township is contemplating modifying the “Home Services District” within the Redevelopment Plan to add bus parking as a permitted use, and to establish bulk standards relating to such use; and WHEREAS, a proposed amendment to the Redevelopment Plan to this effect, dated December 2010, is attached hereto as Exhibit A and by this reference incorporated herein (the “ Proposed Third Amendment ”); and WHEREAS, in accordance with the provisions of N.J.S.A. 40A:12A-7 the Township wishes to utilize the Planning Board's experience and expertise in evaluating the Proposed Third Amendment and determining, among other things, their consistency with the Township's land use and redevelopment goals and objectives for the Downtown Redevelopment Area, NOW THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED by the West Orange Township Council: I. GENERAL The aforementioned recitals are incorporated herein as though fully set forth at length.

II. PLANNING BOARD DIRECTED TO PREPARE REPORT The Township Council hereby authorizes and directs the Planning Board to review the Proposed Third Amendment, and, as provided by N.J.S.A. 40A:12A-7, to transmit a report containing its recommendations to the Township Council within forty-five (45) days. III. SEVERABILITY If any part of this Resolution shall be deemed invalid, such parts shall be severed and the invalidity thereby shall not affect the remaining parts of this Resolution. IV. AVAILABILITY OF THE RESOLUTION A copy of this resolution shall be available for public inspection at the offices of the Township. V. EFFECTIVE DATE This Resolution shall take effect upon final passage. ____________________________________ Honorable Sal M. Anderton Council President ____________________________________ Karen J. Carnevale M unicipal Clerk Dated: December 14, 2010 Approved as to form on the basis of the facts provided: COUNCIL YES NO ABS N.V. AB COUNCIL YES NO ABS N.V. AB Anderton, Pres. Resolution # 338-10 Adopted 12/14/2010 RESOLUTION WHEREAS, on January 19, 2010, the Township Council of the Township of West Orange adopted on second reading Ordinance #2243-09, granting renewal of municipal consent to Comcast of New Jersey II, LLC (“Comcast”), to construct, connect, operate and maintain a cable television and communications system in the Township of West Orange for a term of fifteen (15) years, and WHEREAS, as part of the consideration for the renewal of the Township’s municipal consent, Comcast agreed and promised to provide the Township with a one-time grant for access related need in the amount of $75,000.00, within six (6) months of the renewal Certificate of Approval by the Office of Cable Television, and WHEREAS, the basis of the access related need consisted largely of the testimony of Martin Kale, Media Coordinator for the West Orange Board of Education, regarding the equipment needs for the operation of Channel 36, the Township’s public, educational and governmental access channel, in order to replace and/or upgrade aging equipment to more technologically current and better functioning equipment to maintain a high quality of broadcasting, both for the benefit of the students who receive training in broadcasting and for the benefit of the public by maintaining an acceptable quality of broadcasting, and WHEREAS, the Township has received its grant for access related needs in the amount of $75,000.00, and has received the Board of Education’s Media Coordinator’s list of needed equipment, and wishes to transfer from that grant the sum of $60,000.00, to the West Orange Board of Education specifically to be used for purchase of new equipment to enable and facilitate the effective and efficient operation of Channel 36, the Township’s public, educational and governmental access channel, NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT, AND HEREBY IT IS, RESOLVED BY THE TOWNSHIP COUNCIL OF THE TOWNSHIP OF WEST ORANGE, that the sum of $60,000.00, from the $75,000 grant received from Comcast for access related needs in connection with the renewal of its municipal consent for a term of fifteen (15) years, shall be transferred and paid to the West Orange Board of Education specifically for the purchase of new and upgraded equipment, including, but not limited to, the equipment set forth on the list annexed hereto, to fulfill the access related needs of Channel 36, and to enable and facilitate that Channel’s effective and efficient operation. __________________________________ Sal M. Anderton, Council President __________________________________ Karen Carnevale, Municipal Clerk

337-10 December 14, 2010 R E S O L U T I O N WHEREAS, the Township of West Orange requires bid phase and construction management administration and inspection services for the project known as Downtown West Orange Streetscape and Traffic Improvement Program; and WHEREAS, the services of a Professional Engineering firm will be needed to provide these bid phase and construction management services; and WHEREAS, the firm of Birdsall Engineering, Inc., 611 Industrial Way West, Eatontown, New Jersey 07724 submitted a proposal dated March 31, 2010 for engineering services associated with the bid phase and construction phase services for Downtown West Orange Streetscape and Traffic Improvement Program in the amount of $212,250.00; and WHEREAS, the firm of Birdsall Engineering responded to the Township’s open request for professional engineering services for the period September 1, 2010, to February 28, 2011; and WHEREAS, the firm of Birdsall Engineering, Inc. provided design services for this project; and WHEREAS, there are funds available for these services; and WHEREAS, the Township Council for the Township of West Orange concurs with the foregoing. NOW, THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED by the Township Council of the Township of West Orange that a professional services contract be awarded to Birdsall Engineering, Inc. of 611 Industrial Way West, Eatontown, New Jersey to provide bid phase and construction management, administration and inspection services for Downtown West Orange Streetscape and Traffic Improvement Program in accordance with its proposal dated March 31, 2010 in the amount not to exceed $212,250.00 BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that whereas under the Local Public Contracts Law services to be provided herein are of a professional nature and will not reasonably permit the drawing of specifications or receipt of competitive bids. BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that a copy of this resolution be published in the West Orange
Chronicle as required by law within ten (10) days of its passage. Karen J. Carnevale, Municipal Clerk Sal M. Anderton, Council President Adopted: December 14, 2010

336-10 December 14, 2010 RESOLUTION WHEREAS, the Township of West Orange entered into a contract with A & J Contractors Group, Inc. a Ne w Jersey Corporation having its principal place of business at 105 Federal Road, Monroe Township, New Jersey 08831 for 2009 Phase III Street Improvements- Various Streets; and WHEREAS, the Township Council by Resolution No. 61-10 dated March 9, 2010 awarded a contract for the Base Bid of $749,047.11; and WHEREAS, the Township Council by Resolution No. 274-10 dated October 26, 2010 approved Change Order No. 1 in the amount of $123,326.40: and WHEREAS, the Township Engineer recommended the following amendment to Change Order No. 1 as being necessary and beneficial; and WHEREAS, Change Order No. 1 and final reflects final construction costs and costs expected with additional work to correct unforeseen conditions as shown in the attached Change Order submitted by the contractor and reviewed and approved by the Township Engineer; and WHEREAS, sufficient funds exist to pay for the Change Order amendment; and WHEREAS, the Township Council concurs the foregoing; and NOW, THEREFORE IT BE RESOLVED by the Township Council of the Township of West Orange that amendment to Change Order No. 1 and final in the amount of $11,824.00 with A & J Contractors Group, Inc., 2009 Phase III Street Improvements- Various Streets, is hereby approved and the Township Council further authorizes Leonard R. Lepore, Municipal Engineer to execute said Change Order Amendment. Karen J. Carnevale, Municipal Clerk Sal M. Anderton, Council President Adopted: December 14, 2010

334-10 December 14, 2010 RESOLUTION WHEREAS, the Township Council for the Township of West Orange desires to videotape its regularly scheduled and any special Township Council meetings for viewing by the public on the Township’s public access cable station, TV36; and WHEREAS, the services of a videographer are needed to properly record the Council meetings and prepare them for televising; and WHEREAS, C.J.V.P. LLC, located at 471 Sampton Avenue, South Plainfield, NJ 07080 has personnel with the experience and training as videographers to perform the required services; and WHEREAS, C.J.V.P. LLC, has agreed to provide video graphic services for all regularly scheduled Township Council meetings at a cost of $ 400; and WHEREAS, C.J.V.P. LLC has agreed to provide video graphic services for any additional special meeting of the Township Council at the cost of $150 for the first hour and $75 for each additional hour; and WHEREAS, there are approximately twenty (20) regularly scheduled Council meetings during the calendar year of 201 1; and WHEREAS, C.J.V.P. LLC, has agreed that each shoot will include one professional camera with up to four (4) hours of coverage; and WHEREAS, C.J.V.P. Inc., has agreed that all council meetings for the year will be digitally archived and be made available to the public at the cost of $20.00 per DVD; and WHEREAS, C.J.V.P. LLC, also has agreed that it will be available to do a two camera shoot at no additional charge if the Township determines that same is required because of the holding of a larger than normal meeting; and WHEREAS, C.J.V.P. LLC, understands and agrees that videotaping will ordinarily occur in the Township Council chambers, but may from time to time be done at other locations as identified by the Council President; and WHEREAS, the Council President has the right to cancel any taping session at no charge to the Township up until 3:00 p.m. on the day of the Township Council meetings. Meeting dates may be changed and additional meetings added at the sole discretion of the Council President; and WHEREAS, C.J.V.P. LLC, shall arrive and set up at the meeting location at least thirty (30) minutes before each meeting is scheduled to begin and shall be prepared to commence taping at the beginning of each meeting; and WHEREAS, C.J.V.P. LLC, agrees to (i) provide the original digital tape of each meeting to the Public Information Officer no later than seven (7) days after the meeting; (ii) deliver a SVHS tape of each meeting to Mr. Marty Kale at the Media Center with a Program Time Request Form provided by the Public Information Officer, by 2:30 p.m. on the Wednesday following the Council meeting, and further (iii) deliver a VHS tape of each meeting to the Municipal Clerk’s Office at the same date and time; and WHEREAS, C.J.V.P. LLC agrees to follow the same procedures for videotaping special meetings of the Township Council, except, except that delivery of the SVHS tape shall be made to the Media Center at the High school b efore 2:20 pm on the second open school day after taping; and WHEREAS, the Township Council and C.J.V.P. LLC shall each have the right to terminate this contract upon thirty (30) days written notice to C.J.V.P. LLC at 471 Sampton Avenue, South Plainfield, New Jersey 07080 and the Township c/o Municipal Clerk, 66 main Street, West Orange, New Jersey 07052; and WHEREAS, C.J.V.P. LLC agrees to provide an emergency phone number to the Municipal Clerk for use in the event of emergencies or other inquiries/issues which may arise, agrees to promptly notify the Council President and Municipal Clerk in the event any technical or other issues arises, and agrees and understands that the videotape of each meeting must be of sufficient quality to be seen and heard on the cable access channel, free of static and interference, and in a quality similar to normal television shows; and

WHEREAS, C.J.V.P. LLC agrees that in the event a representative is not available for any given Council meeting or the company’s equipment is not functional, C.J.V.P. LLC agrees to and will obtain the services of a replacement videographer at no additional charge to the Township; and WHEREAS, the total expenditure for this Agreement is below the threshold of the Local Public Contracts Law and the New Jersey Pay to Play Law; NOW, BE IT HEREBY RESOLVED by the Township Council of the Township of West Orange that the Township be and hereby is authorized to engage C.J.V.P. LLC as videographer for West Orange Township Council meetings for the period between January 1, 2011 and December 31, 2011 at the cost of $400 per regular Township Council meeting and $150 for the first hour of any Special Township Council meeting and $75 for each additional hour during a Special Township Council meeting. I HEREBY AGREE TO THE TERMS AND CONDITIONS SET FORTH IN THE ABOVE RESOLUTION. I UNDERSTAND THE TERMS AND AGREE TO BE BOUND BY THEM. Karen J. Carnevale Sal M. Anderton Municipal Clerk Council President Adopted: December 14, 2010

321-10 December 14, 2010 RESOLUTION WHEREAS, for many years the Rock Spring Club (“the Club”), located at 90 Rock Spring Road, West Orange, NJ 07052, has arranged for a small helicopter to land on the grounds of the Club to deliver Santa Claus to Club members and their guests in attendance for a holiday celebration; WHERAS, this year’s annual Santa Claus event is scheduled for Sunday, December 12, 20 10. WHERAS, Santa’s reindeer, Rudolph et als., are not available for the trip at this time of year as they must be well -rested in preparation for their big Christmas Eve event; and WHERAS, Santa Claus has again graciously managed to make arrangements to travel by small helicopter to attend the Club’s annual holiday celebration; and WHERAS, the New Jersey Department of Transportation, Division of Aeronautics, Inspection & Aircraft Operation, not wanting to be Scrooge-like, does permit and has in the past permitted helicopter landings such as these on country club property when approved pursuant to its application process; and WHERAS, the helicopter pilot as agent for the Club, will prepare the required Application for Temporary Aeronautical Facility License for submission to the New Jersey Department of Transportation, which must be delivered no later than December 10, 20 10, and which must be accompanied by, among other documents and things which the Club will provide, a “letter, statement, or certificate from the appropriate governing body which states there is no objection to the issuance of a temporary license (mandatory for all temps)”; and WHERAS, for this event, the appropriate body is the Township Council of the Township of West Orange; and WHERAS, in order to accommodate the Club, and relying upon the Club’s experience with this tradition and its assurance that all appropriate security and safety precautions will be taken, the Council President and Members have communicated by telephone and e-mail and have unanimously voted to approve and adopt this Resolution in advance of the next regularly scheduled Council meeting in order that Rock Spring Club can include it as an attachment to its application as required and continue this holiday tradition; NOW, THEREFOR, BE IT RESOLVED, that the West Orange Township Council, the governing body for the Township of West Orange, New Jersey, does and hereby states that it has no objection to the issuance of a Temporary Aeronautical Facility License to the Rock Spring Club, located at 90 Rock Spring Road, West Orange, NJ 07052, for the purpose of permitting transportation and delivery of Santa Claus to the Club at approximately 2:00 p.m., on Sunday, December 1 2, 20 10, for participation in the Club’s traditional Christmas celebration. Sal M. Anderton, Council President Karen J. Carnevale, Municipal Clerk Adopted: 12/ 9 /10 Memorialized: 12/14/10

pages.text: 3 2 0 -10 December 14, 2010 RESOLUTION TO HOLD A CLOSED SESSION WHEREAS, the Open Public Meetings Act (N.J.S.A. 10:4. et seq.) provides for the exclusion of the public meetings of the governing body during the discussion of certain matters; and WHEREAS, prior to the exclusion of the public from a meeting of the Township Council it is required that the Council adopt a Resolution stating the general nature of the subject to be discussed and stating as precisely as possible the time when the minutes of the discussion conducted in closed session can be disclosed to the public; and WHERE AS, this body is about to consider a matter which falls within the purview of N.J.S.A. 10 -4-12, and can properly exclude the public from such discussions; now, therefore, be it BE IT RESOLVED, that the Township Council of the Township of West Orange, now assembled in public session at its regular meeting of December 14, 2010 shall enter into a closed session to consider the following matter(s). ( ) 1. Discussion of any material, the disclosure of which constitutes an invasion of individual privacy.. ( ) 2. A collective bargaining agreement or the terms of provisions of same. ( ) 3. Techniques or tactic utilized to protect the safety and property of the public provided that their disclosure could impair such protection. ( ) 4. An investigation of violations o r possible violations of the laws of the State of New Jersey and/ or the Township of West Orange Administrative Code. ( X ) 5. Pending or anticipated litigation or contract negotiation in which this body is or maybe a party. ( ) 6. A matter falling within the attorney-client privilege to the extent that confidentiality is r equired in order for the attorney to exercise his ethical duties to this body. () 7. Personnel matters. ( ) 8. Discussion of any matter which by express provision of Federal law or State statute or rule of Court shall be rendered confidential. ( ) 9. Discussion of any matter in which the release of information would impair a right to receive funds from the Government of the United Sates. ( ) 10. Discussion of any matter involving the purchase, lease or acquisition of real property with public funds, the setting of banking rates or investment of public funds, where it could adversely affect the public interest if discussion of such matters were disclosed. ( ) 11. Deliberations occurring after a public hearing that may result in imposition of a civil penalty or suspension or loss of a license or permit. More specifically, the Council may discuss in closed session the following topic ( s ):

Seton Hall Preparatory School Occidental Litigation ACLU Litigation Llewellyn Park (the general subject matters) of discussion shall be indicated by a check mark in the appropriate box and shall be more specifically referred to thereafter to the extent suc h additional disclosure can be made without compromising the need for confidentiality giving rise to the closed session. IT IS FURTH E R RESOLVED, that the minutes of said discussion shall be made public as soon as the matter under discussion is no longer of a confidential or sensitive nature such that the public interest will no longer be served by such confidentiality. The foregoing Resolution was duly adopted by the Township Council of the Township of West Orange at a public meeting held on December 14, 2010 Motion: Second: Vote: Opposed: Karen J. 450269.4 313-10 December 14, 2010 R ESOLUTION OF THE TOWNSHIP OF WEST ORANGE, IN THE COUNTY OF ESSEX, NEW JERSEY, AUTHORIZING THE EXECUTION OF A PROFESSIONAL SERVICES CONTRACT WHEREAS, the Township of West Orange (the “Township”) wishes to procure professional financial advisory services in relation to the evaluation of redevelopment and rehabilitation programs within the Township; and WHEREAS, NW Financial Group, L.L.C. (the “Consultant”) has provided such professional financial advisory services to a number of municipalities and other governmental entities across the State; and WHEREAS, the Township desires to engage the Consultant to provide professional financial advisory services as described above; and WHEREAS, pursuant to N.J.S.A. 40A:11-5, the Township may enter into contracts for professional services, NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED BY THE TOWNSHIP COUNCIL OF THE TOWNSHIP OF WEST ORANGE, IN THE COUNTY OF ESSEX, NEW JERSEY, AS FOLLOWS: I. GENERAL The aforementioned recitals are incorporated herein as though fully set forth at length. II. AUTHORIZATION TO EXECUTE CONTRACT FOR SERVICES The Township Council hereby authorizes the Mayor and/or the Business Administrator (each an "Authorized Official") to execute a contract for professional financial advisory services with NW Financial Group, L.L.C., Jersey City, New Jersey in substantially the form attached hereto as Exhibit A (the “Contract”) together with such additions, deletions, or modifications as may be necessary in consultation with legal counsel to effectuate the terms of the C ontract. III. CONTRACT AMOUNT NOT TO EXCEED $25,000 Payments under the Contract shall not exceed the amount of $25,000 in the aggregate without further authorization of the Township, which amounts shall be paid solely from the redevelopers ’ funded escrow account. IV. SEVERABILITY If any part of this Resolution shall be deemed invalid, such parts shall be severed and the invalidity thereby shall not affect the remaining parts of this Resolution. V. AVAILABILITY OF THE RESOLUTION A copy of this Resolution shall be available for public inspection at the offices of the Township. VI. EFFECTIVE DATE This Resolution shall take effect upon final passage. Karen J. Carnevale Sal M. Anderton Municipal Clerk Council President Adopted: December 14, 2010

documents.title: APPROVING SETTLEMENT

pages.text: 312-10 December 14, 2010 RESOLUTION APPROVING SETTLEMENT WHEREAS, West Orange resident Paul Tractenberg ("Mr. Tractenberg") filed two requests pursuant to the Open Public Records Act; N.J.S.A. 47:1A-1.2 ("OPRA"); and WHEREAS, Mr. Tractenberg requests copies of certain appraisals concerning the tract of land owned by West Essex Highlands, Inc.; WHEREAS, the Township asserted that the appraisals were subject to the deliberative exemption under OPRA; and WHEREAS, Mr. Tractenberg commenced an action in lieu of prerogative writs under OPRA seeking access to the appraisals; and WHEREAS, the Superior Court of New Jersey, Law Division conducted a trial and determined that the full unredacted appraisals were not available under OPRA; and WHEREAS, Mr. Tractenberg filed an appeal to the Superior Court of New Jersey, Appellate Division; and WHEREAS, on September 16, 2010, the Appellate Division issued its opinion wherein it determined that the appraisals were subject to release under OPRA, 416 N.J. Super. 354 (App. Div. 2010); and WHEREAS, Mr. Tractenberg's counsel, Richard Gutman, Esq., has submitted fee applications to the Appellate Division and the Law Division based upon the prevailing party provisions of OPRA; and WHEREAS, the total amount sought by Mr. Gutman in excess of $150,564; and WHEREAS, the Township Attorney has negotiated with Mr. Gutman in an attempt to resolve all pending litigation including the application for fees and expenses; and WHEREAS, after various negotiations, Mr. Gutman has agreed to resolve all claims upon payment of $69,500 no later than December 31, 2010; and WHEREAS, the Township has made the necessary fund transfers to satisfy this

settlement; and WHEREAS, the Township desires to resolve this matter once and for all without any further risk or expense; NOW, BE IT HEREBY RESOLVED, by the Township Council of Township of West Orange that the Township Attorney be and is hereby authorized to resolve any and all claims by Paul Tractenberg and Richard Gutman, Esq. upon payment of $69,500 in full satisfaction upon receipt of general releases from Mr. Tractenberg and Mr. Gutman including a waiver of any and all claims and expenses under any other statute, ordinance, rule or law; and it is further RESOLVED, that the Business Administrator be and is hereby authorized to take such steps and actions as is necessary and appropriate to implement this Resolution. Karen J. Carnevale, Municipal Clerk Sal M. Anderton, Council President Adopted: December 14, 2010

pages.text: 3 02-10 November 23, 2010 RESOLUTION MUNICIPAL PAYROLL SERVICES WHEREAS, the Township of West Orange (the “Township”) needs to retain a contractor qualified to handle the Township s weekly payroll services; and WHEREAS, the Township issued a Request for Proposal (“RFP”) in accordance with the Competitive Contracting Process (N.J.S.A. 40A:11-4.4 et seq.) for the Municipal Payroll Services; and WHEREAS, on November 17, 2010 the Township received three (3) responses to its RFP from Action Data Services, Balance Point and Casa Payroll Services; and WHEREAS, the three (3) proposals were reviewed and evaluated by the Evaluation Committee consisting of the Chief Financial Officer, Purchasing Agent, Payroll Clerks, and IT Department (the Evaluation Committee”); and WHEREAS, after evaluating the proposals under the criteria of technology, Functionality, Accountability, Service, Pricing, and RFP com pliance as set forth in section ( 2 ) of the RFP entitled Evaluation of Proposals, the Evaluation Committee prepared an evaluation report and recommended that Balance Point be awarded the contract for Municipal Payroll Services. The amount of award, including first year’s implementation, is not to exceed $ 43, 568.06. The Township is allowed through the L ocal P ublic C ontracts L aw to extend this contract a total of two more one year terms, each subsequent term will not exceed $42,067.06; and WHEREAS, pursuant to N.J.S.A. 40A:11-4.5(d) a report was prepared by the Evaluation Committee and filed with the Clerk on November 18, 2010, at least 48 hours prior to award and made available for public inspection; and WHEREAS, the Chief Financial Officer has prepared and filed a certification of funds indicating that funds are available for this contract. NOW, BE IT HEREBY RESOLVED, by the Council of the Township of West Orange that the contract for the Municipal Payroll Services is awarded to Balance Point, 65 Harristown Road, Suite 302, Glen Rock, NJ 07401. BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that the Mayor be and hereby authorized to execute the contract between the Township of West Orange and Balance Point, for Municipal Payroll Services within the terms set forth; and RESOLVED, that this contract is awarded as a competitive contract in accordance with the Local Public Contract Law; and RESOLVED, that the original contract between the Township of West Orange and Balance Point shall be maintained in the Municipal Clerk’s Office. _____________________________ __________________________ Karen J. Carnevale Honorable Sal Anderton Township Clerk Council President Adopted: November 23, 2010

THIS AGREEMENT, made this 23 rd day of November 2010 by and between: TOWNSHIP OF WEST ORANGE, a municipal corporation of the State of New Jersey, having its principal offices at 66 Main Street, West Orange, New Jersey, hereinafter referred to as "Township"; and WEST ORANGE COMMUNITY HOUSE, a nonprofit corporation of the State of New Jersey having its principal offices at 242 Main Street, West Orange, New Jersey, hereinafter referred to as "Contractor". W I T N E S E T H: WHEREAS, the Township desires to provide certain recreational services, social services, activities, and facilities to the residents of the Township of West Orange; and WHEREAS, it is the purpose of this agreement to recite the terms and conditions under which the foregoing shall be provided; and NOW THEREFORE, in consideration of the foregoing and of the mutual covenants hereinafter stated, the parties do hereby agree as follows:

1. For the period of January 1, 2010 to December 31, 2010 Contractor shall provide and make available to West Orange residents, services and facilities for participation by such residents of West Orange. 2. The foregoing facilities and services shall be supervised and operated by personnel provided by Contractor, which personnel shall be solely the employees of Contractor, who is responsible to pay them. 3. Contractor shall provide, at Contractor's expense, Workers Compensation Insurance, covering its employees performing hereunder, and public liability insurance with limits of Five Hundred Thousand ($500,000.00) Dollars to One Million ($1,000,000.00) Dollars for the areas and locations where the recreational facilities are conducted. Said insurance shall cover the interest of the Township and shall be with carriers satisfactory to the Township and authorized to do business in New Jersey. Certificates evidencing the foregoing shall be furnished to the Township upon execution of this Agreement. 4. Contractor agrees to indemnify the Township and save it harmless, including Township's employees, agents and servants, from and against any and all losses, claims, liabilities and expenses which may arise or be claimed

against the Township, its agents, servants or employees in connection with any phase of this Agreement. 5. Neither this Agreement nor the monies to grow hereunder may be assigned. 6. Contractor acknowledges that it has read N.J.S.A. 10:2-1, et seq., of the Revised Statutes of the State of New Jersey (Discrimination in Employment on Public Works, Contract Provisions), the terms of which are incorporated herein as though expressly set forth at length. Contractor agrees to comply with and be bound by the provisions thereof. 7. It is understood that this Agreement shall be deemed effective as of January 1, 2010. 8. Details of the facilities and programs involved herein shall be furnished to the Director of the Department of Recreation of the Township; and, a year-end report, as to all of same, shall likewise be furnished to said Director prior to December 31, 2010. 9. All programs provided hereunder shall be under the joint overall supervision of the Director of the Department of Recreation of Township and Director or Contractor. They shall jointly supervise all of said programs, regarding which there shall be the right of modification and substitution with other programs subject to joint approval of Director of Contractor and Director of the Department of Recreation of

Township. The location, dates and scheduling involved shall be subject to the joint approval of Director of Contractor and Director of Department of Recreation of Township. 10. Township shall pay to Contractor for the services to be provided hereunder for the full one-year term, the sum of Forty-Five Thousand ($45,000.00) Dollars. 11. The manner of payment shall be as determined jointly by the Director of Contractor and Director of the Department of Recreation of Township. No payment hereunder shall issue unless the Director of the Department of Recreation of Township has filed with the Business Administrator of the Township, a written statement certifying that the payment should issue based upon his knowledge of performance hereunder or performance in progress hereunder. 12. The parties hereto agree that the provisions of the "New Jersey Prevailing Wage Act" shall apply hereto. Accordingly, contractor agrees to comply with the provisions of N.J.S.A. 34:11-56.25 through 34:11-56.33, the provisions of which are hereby incorporated by reference as though stated at length herein. Contractor hereby declares that it is aware of the prevailing wage rates on file in the Township Hall of Township pursuant to said Act and agrees to comply therewith. Contractor further agrees as follows: A. All employees of contractor performing services

hereunder shall be paid not less than the prevailing wage rate as specified. B. Contractor shall maintain accurate records, showing name, kind of work performed and actual hourly rate of wages paid to each employee employed hereunder. Such records shall be maintained for three (3) years from date of payment and shall be available for inspection by the Township's Business Administrator or his designee on request. C. Contractor shall post the prevailing wage rate for each employee performing work hereunder, as determined by the Commissioner of Labor and Industry of the State of New Jersey, including the effective date of any changes thereof, in a prominent and easily accessible place and the principal Office of Contractor. D. If it is found that any employee of Contractor is paid less than the required wage rates Township may, on written notice to Contractor, terminate Contractor's rights to proceed hereunder, or as to such portion of services rendered hereunder as to which there has been a failure to pay the required wages. Township may then arrange to prosecute the rendering of the services hereunder by other means, in which even Contractor shall be liable to Township for all costs and damages incurred by Township. E. It is specifically understood that the provisions of

this paragraph shall not apply to such persons engaged by Contract render services hereunder who are performing such services as volunteers without remuneration. F. Contractor agrees to be bound by the provisions of Schedule A attached hereto and made a part hereof. IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the parties have caused these presents to be signed by their proper corporate officers and their property corporate seals to be hereto affixed the day and year first above written. ATTEST: TOWNSHIP OF WEST ORANGE ________________________ __________________________ Karen J. Carnevale BY: ROBERT D. PARISI, MAYOR Township Clerk ATTEST: WEST ORANGE COMMUNITY HOUSE _________________________ BY:________________________ SECRETARY PRESIDENT

"SCHEDULE A" (I) During the performance of this contract the contractor agrees as follows: a. The contractor or subcontractor, where applicable, will not discriminate against any employee of applicant for employment because of age, race, creed, color, national, origin, ancestry, marital status or sex. The contractor will take affirmative action to ensure that such applicants are recruited and employed, and that employees are treated during employment, without regard to their age, race, creed, color, national origin, ancestry, marital status or sex. Such action shall include, but not be limited to the following: employment, upgrading, demotion, or transfer; recruitment or recruitment advertising; layoff or termination; rates of pay or other forms of compensation; and selection for training, including apprenticeship. The contractor agrees to post in conspicuous places, available to employees and applicants for employment, notices to be provided by the Public Agency Compliance Officer setting forth provisions of this non- discrimination clause; b. The contractor or subcontractor, where applicable will, in all solicitations or advertisements for employees placed by or on behalf of the contractor, state that all

qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to age, creed, color, national origin, ancestry, martial status or sex; c. The contractor or subcontractor, where applicable, will send to each labor union or representative or workers with which it has a collective bargaining agreement or other contract or understanding, a notice, to be provided by the agency contracting officer advising the labor union or worker's representative of the contractor's commitments under this act and shall post copies of the notice in conspicuous places available to employees and applicants for employment. d. The contractor or subcontractor, where applicable, agrees to comply with any regulations promulgated by the treasurer pursuant to P.L. 1975,c.127, as amended and supplemented from time to time. (II) The contractor or subcontractor agrees to attempt in good faith to employ minority and female workers consistent with the applicable county employment goals prescribed by section 5.2 of the Regulations promulgated by the Treasurer pursuant to P.L. 1975, c.127, as amended and supplemented from time to time or in accordance with a binding determination of the applicable county employment goals determined by the Affirmative Action Office pursuant to

section 5.2 of the Regulations promulgated by the Treasurer pursuant to P.L. 1975, c. 127, as amended and supplemented from time to time. (III) The contractor or subcontractor agrees to inform in writing appropriate recruitment agencies in the area, including employment agencies, placements bureaus, colleges, universities, labor unions, that it does not discriminate on the basis of age, creed, color, national origin, ancestry, marital status or sex, and that it will discontinue the use of any recruitment agency which engages in direct or indirect or indirect discriminatory practices. (IV) The Contractor or subcontractor agrees to revise any of its testing procedure, if necessary, to assure that all personnel testing conforms with the principles of job-related testing, as established by the statutes and court decisions of the State of New Jersey and as established by applicable federal law and applicable federal court decisions. (V) The contractor or subcontractor agrees to review all procedures relating to transfer, upgrading, downgrading and layoff to ensure that all such actions are taken without regard to age, creed, color, national origin, ancestry, marital status or sex, and conform with the applicable employment goals, consistent with the statutes and court decisions of the State of New Jersey, and applicable federal
Law and applicable federal court decisions.

pages.text: 2 8 9 -10 November 4, 2010 RESOLUTION TO HOLD A CLOSED SESSION WHEREAS, the Open Public Meetings Act (N.J.S.A. 10:4. et seq.) provides for the exclusion of the public meetings of the governing body during the discussion of certain matters; and WHEREAS, prior to the exclusion of the public from a meeting of the Township Council it is required that the Council adopt a Resolution stating the general nature of the subject to be discussed and stating as precisely as possible the time when the minutes of the discussion conducted in closed session can be disclosed to the public; and WHERE AS, this body is about to consider a matter which falls within the purview of N.J.S.A. 10 -4-12, and can properly exclude the public from such discussions; now, therefore, be it BE IT RESOLVED, that the Township Council of the Township of West Orange, now assembled in public session at its regular meeting of November 4, 2010 shall enter into a closed session to consider the following matter(s). ( ) 1. Discussion of any material, the disclosure of which constitutes an invasion of individual privacy.. ( ) 2. A collective bargaining agreement or the terms of provisions of same. ( ) 3. Techniques or tactic utilized to protect the safety and property of the public provided that their disclosure could impair such protection. ( ) 4. An investigation of violations o r possible violations of the laws of the State of New Jersey and/ or the Township of West Orange Administrative Code. ( X ) 5. Pending or anticipated litigation or contract negotiation in which this body is or maybe a party. ( ) 6. A matter falling within the attorney-client privilege to the extent that confidentiality is r equired in order for the attorney to exercise his ethical duties to this body. () 7. Personnel matters. ( ) 8. Discussion of any matter which by express provision of Federal law or State statute or rule of Court shall be rendered confidential. ( ) 9. Discussion of any matter in which the release of information would impair a right to receive funds from the Government of the United Sates. ( ) 10. Discussion of any matter involving the purchase, lease or acquisition of real property with public funds, the setting of banking rates or investment of public funds, where it could adversely affect the public interest if discussion of such matters were disclosed. ( ) 11. Deliberations occurring after a public hearing that may result in imposition of a civil penalty or suspension or loss of a license or permit. More specifically, the Council may discuss in closed session the following topics:

pages.text: 282-10 October 26, 2010 RESOLUTION AUTHORIZING A WINDOW CONTRACT FOR VARIOUS GOODS AND SERVICES WHEREAS, the Township of West Orange wants to hire a computer software designer to customize a software application; and WHEREAS, this application will be part of the westorange.org website and will be available for residents to use as a tool to access various Township departments and will also serve as a tool for the Township to resolve issues in a timely manner and retain statistical information for our database; and WHEREAS, a request for a quote was sent to three companies and the design received from Frank Gibbons Services for in the amount of $20,000.00 was reviewed for its technical merit and complies with our specification, and WHEREAS, pursuant to the provisions of N.J.S.A. 19:44A-20.4 et seq., when the cost of goods and/or services that fall between $ 17,500.00 and the bid threshold of $ 36,000.00 in the aggregate, an approval by resolution must be in place prior to contract; and W HEREAS, the above named business or businesses have completed and submitted a Business Entity Disclosure Certification which certifies the business entity has not made any reportable contributions to a political or candidate committee in the Township of West Orange in the previous one year, and that the contract will prohibit the above named vendors from making any reportable contributions through the term of the contract. NOW THEREFORE, BE IT RESOL V ED that the Council of the Township of West authorizes the Purchasing Agent on behalf of the Township to issue and execute a Purchase Order for the foregoing, with funds certified available by the Chief Financial Officer; and BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that the Business Administrator is hereby authorized to arrange to pay for the foregoing in accordance with the terms of the purchase order. BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that the Business Disclosure Entity Certification and the Determination of V alue be placed on file with this resolution and notice of this award will be published in accordance with the applicable law. Karen J. Carnevale, Municipal Clerk Honorable Sal M. Anderton Council President Adopted: October 26, 2010

NOW THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED by the Township Council of the Township of West Orange that an additional appropriation of $375,000 be authorized as Change Order No. 3 for the contract 2009 Phase IV Street Improvements – Various Streets” with DLS Contracting, Inc. of 633 Franklin Avenue, Nutley, New jersey to continue work in accordance with that

contract at the unit prices bid under Alternate “E”. Karen J. Carnevale Honorable Sal M. Anderton Township Clerk Council President Adopted: October 26, 2010 Approved as to form on the basis of the facts provided:

280-10 October 26, 2010 R E S O L U T I O N WHEREAS, in June 1993 the Township of West Orange removed three underground storage tanks at property known as Fire House No. 4 at 280 Pleasant Valley Way; and WHEREAS, during their removal, representatives of the PMK Group who prepared the closure plan found evidence that all three tanks leaked; and WHEREAS, the Remedial Investigation Report prepared by the PMK Group found soil contamination at the location of the gasoline storage tank which exceeded the New Jersey Department of Environmental Protection (NJDEP) Groundwater Soil Cleanup Criteria; and WHEREAS, the PMK Group prepared a Remedial Investigation Work plan which was approved by the NJDEP; and WHEREAS, the PMK Group implemented the requirements of the Remedial Investigation Work plan and subsequently prepared a Remedial Investigation Report dated February 6, 2008; and WHEREAS, the NJDEP letter dated June 25, 2008 and the Remedial Action Work plan Addendum approved by the NJDEP on August 6, 2008 require additional remedial investigative work consisting of vapor intrusion investigation, high vacuum extraction, groundwater sampling and regulatory reporting; and WHEREAS, the Birdsall Services (formerly PMK Group) of 65 Jackson Drive, Cranford, New Jersey submitted a proposal dated June 2, 2010 to perform these additional services to address the requirements of the NJDEP for a fee not to exceed $89,500.00.; and WHEREAS, the PMK Group responded to the Township’s open request for Professional Services in February 2010; and WHEREAS, the Township Engineer recommends Birdsall Services Group be awarded a Professional Services Contract in conformance with their proposal of June 2, 2010; and WHEREAS, the Township Council concurs in the foregoing. NOW, THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED by the Township Council of the Township of West Orange that a Professional Services Contract be awarded to Birdsall Services Group of 65 Jackson Drive, P.O. Box 5000, Cranford, New Jersey 07016 to perform the services outlined in accordance with their proposal dated June 2, 2010 in an amount not to exceed $89,500.00. BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that whereas under the Local Public Contracts Law the services to be provided herein are of a professional nature and will not reasonably permit the drawing of specifications or receipt of competitive bids, the Township Council of the Township of West Orange hereby authorizes a contract for these services with Birdsall Services Group, 65 Jackson Drive, P.O. Box 5000, Cranford, New Jersey 07016.

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that the award of these professional services to the Birdsall Services Group is made pursuant to their response to the Township’s open request for professional services of February 2010. BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that a copy of this Resolution be published in the West Orange Chronicle as required by law within (10) days of its passage. Karen J. Carnevale Honorable Sal M. Anderton Township Clerk Council President Adopted: October 26, 2010 Approved as to form on the basis of the facts provided:

pages.text: 279-10 October 26, 2010 RESOLUTION AUTHORIZING COMPETITIVE CONTRACTING PROCESS FOR PAYROLL PROCESSING SERVICES WHEREAS, the Township will need to secure a company to process the payroll services that has been formerly incorporated in our banking services; and WHEREAS, the cost of these services will exceed the Township bid threshold; and WHEREAS, under the Local Public Contracts Law N.J.S.A. 40A:11-4.1 competitive contracting may be used by local contracting units in lieu of the standard public bidding process for procurement of specialized goods and services where the price exceeds the bid threshold; and WHEREAS, the Township meets the criteria of Local Public Contracts Law N.J.S.A. 40a:11-4.1.3 which allows the use of a methodology to rank and evaluate proposals received to not only secure the best price but the best service to suit the Townships needs. 263-10 October 12, 2010 R E S O L U T I O N WHEREAS, the Township Council by Resolution No. 162-10 dated June 29, 2010 authorized the Municipal Engineer to negotiate a contract or contracts on a emergency basis pursuant to N.J.S.A. 40A:11-6 to eliminate the overflow of sanitary sewage into the basements of homes at 3 and 5 Lessing Court through the installation of individual ejector systems; and WHEREAS, the Municipal Engineer’s estimate of the cost for this work was $37,500.00 per property for a total of $75,000.00; and WHEREAS, the cost proposal submitted by Rocco Ciufalo Plumbing and Heating LLC of 247-251 Watchung Avenue, West Orange, N.J. 07052 to install two individual ejector systems at 3 and 5 Lessing Court is $79,500.00; and WHEREAS, the additional cost is due to the greater depth of the pump chambers and the greater depth of the connection of the pump discharges to the sanitary sewer main than originally anticipated; and WHEREAS, the Township Engineer by letter dated October 5, 2010 recommends the additional appropriation of $4,500.00; and WHERAS, the Township Council concurs in the foregoing. NOW THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED by the Township Council of the Township of West Orange that an additional $4,500.00 be appropriated to eliminate sanitary sewage overflows at 3 and 5 Lessing Court bringing the total appropriation authorized on an emergency basis for this work pursuant to N.J.S.A. 40A:11-6 to $79,500.00. SAL M. ANDERTON, COUNCIL PRESIDENT KAREN J. CARNEVALE, MUNICIPAL CLERK Adopted: October 12, 2010

262-10 October 12, 2010 R E S O L U T I O N WHEREAS, the West Orange Township Council upon the recommendation of the Township Engineer approved Resolution No. 234-10 on September 14, 2010 which authorized an emergency appropriation of $136,811.50 to Grabowski Construction, Inc. of 770 Northfield Avenue, West Orange, N.J. for the emergency reconstruction of the Township’s original easterly interceptor sewer on Valley Road near Kingsley Street; and WHEREAS, upon completion of the work and the authorization of the emergency appropriation, Grabowski Construction, Inc. was invoiced an additional $1,096.00 for Police Traffic Control that was not included on the original invoice of $136,811.50; and WHEREAS, the Township Engineer reviewed the records of the Police Department and the invoices of Grabowski Construction, Inc. and verified that the Police Traffic Director hours included in this invoice were not previously billed; and WHEREAS, the Township Engineer by letter dated October 5, 2010 recommends Grabowski Construction, Inc. be paid for this traffic control; and WHEREAS, the Township Council concurs in the foregoing. NOW THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED by the Township Council of the Township of West Orange that an additional appropriation of $1,096.00 be authorized for Grabowski Construction, Inc. of 770 Northfield Avenue, West Orange, N.J. for Police Traffic Directors associated with the reconstruction of the easterly interceptor sewer on Valley Road bring the final cost to $137,907.50. SAL M. ANDERTON, COUNCIL PRESIDENT KAREN J. CARNEVALE, MUNICIPAL CLERK Adopted: October 12, 2010

pages.text: 2 58 -10 October 12, 2010 RESOLUTION TO HOLD A CLOSED SESSION WHEREAS, the Open Public Meetings Act (N.J.S.A. 10:4. et seq.) provides for the exclusion of the public meetings of the governing body during the discussion of certain matters; and WHEREAS, prior to the exclusion of the public from a meeting of the Township Council it is required that the Council adopt a Resolution stating the general nature of the subject to be discussed and stating as precisely as possible the time when the minutes of the discussion conducted in closed session can be disclosed to the public; and WHERE AS, this body is about to consider a matter which falls within the purview of N.J.S.A. 10 -4-12, and can properly exclude the public from such discussions; now, therefore, be it BE IT RESOLVED, that the Township Council of the Township of West Orange, now assembled in public session at its regular meeting of October 12, 2010 shall enter into a closed session to consider the following matter(s). ( ) 1. Discussion of any material, the disclosure of which constitutes an invasion of individual privacy.. ( ) 2. A collective bargaining agreement or the terms of provisions of same. ( ) 3. Techniques or tactic utilized to protect the safety and property of the public provided that their disclosure could impair such protection. ( ) 4. An investigation of violations o r possible violations of the laws of the State of New Jersey and/ or the Township of West Orange Administrative Code. ( X ) 5. Pending or anticipated litigation or contract negotiation in which this body is or maybe a party. ( ) 6. A matter falling within the attorney-client privilege to the extent that confidentiality is r equired in order for the attorney to exercise his ethical duties to this body. () 7. Personnel matters. ( ) 8. Discussion of any matter which by express provision of Federal law or State statute or rule of Court shall be rendered confidential. ( ) 9. Discussion of any matter in which the release of information would impair a right to receive funds from the Government of the United Sates. ( ) 10. Discussion of any matter involving the purchase, lease or acquisition of real property with public funds, the setting of banking rates or investment of public funds, where it could adversely affect the public interest if discussion of such matters were disclosed. ( ) 11. Deliberations occurring after a public hearing that may result in imposition of a civil penalty or suspension or loss of a license or permit. More specifically, the Council may discuss in closed session the following topics:

One or more matters of Litigation: Tractenberg v. Township of West Orange (the general subject matters) of discussion shall be indicated by a check mark in the appropriate box and shall be more specifically referred to thereafter to the extent suc h additional disclosure can be made without compromising the need for confidentiality giving rise to the closed session. IT IS FURTH E R RESOLVED, that the minutes of said discussion shall be made public as soon as the matter under discussion is no longer of a confidential or sensitive nature such that the public interest will no longer be served by such confidentiality. The foregoing Resolution was duly adopted by the Township Council of the Township of West Orange at a public meeting held on October 12, 2010 Motion: Second: Vote: In Favor: Opposed: Karen J. Carnevale Honorable Sal M. Anderton M unicipal Clerk Council President Adopted: October 12, 2010

256-10 September 28, 2010 RESOLUTION WHEREAS, Crestmont Country Club ("CCC") owns certain property known as Block 174, Lots 1 and 1.01 commonly known as 750 Eagle Rock Avenue in the Township of West Orange ("Properties"); and WHEREAS, CCC filed certain tax appeals for the years 2007 through 2010 carried under Docket Nos. 004628-2007, 006567-2008, 001741-2009, and 001061-2010; and WHEREAS, CCC filed a Woodland Management Plan for various years beginning in 1994; and WHEREAS, CCC sought and obtained a subdivision in 2007; and WHEREAS, the Tax Assessor for the Township of West Orange denied CCC's farmland assessment applications; and WHEREAS, the Township's 2010 assessment for the Properties is $8,781,500 which equalizes to a fair market value of $39,287,593; and WHEREAS, the New Jersey Department of Environmental Protection approved the Woodland Management Plans; and WHEREAS, on February 23, 2010, the Tax Court issued a Letter Opinion denying CCC's Motion for Summary Judgment without prejudice and scheduling a hearing concerning certain issues; and WHEREAS, the Township believes the within Resolution is appropriate, fair and equitable; and WHEREAS, the Township's Tax Assessor, appraisal expert and special real estate tax counsel, Blau & Blau, have recommended the within settlement; NOW THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED BY THE TOWNSHIP COUNCIL OF THE TOWNSHIP OF WEST ORANGE, as follows: 1. All present tax appeals concerning Crestmont Country Club will be settled with reductions in the assessment to be fixed by the West Orange Tax Assessor that result in a total 2007-2010 tax reduction of $1,425,000 with payments/credits to be made as follows: (a) Within twenty (20) days of receipt of CCC's 2010 fourth quarter tax payment, a tax refund will be issued to CCC and Brach Eichler, LLC, CCC's counsel, in the amount of $150,000; and (b) CCC will receive an annual tax credit of $300,000 for tax years 2011, 2012, 2013 and 2014 ("Period") whereby each of the sixteen (16) quarterly tax payments due for the Period shall be reduced by a credit of $75,000; and (c) CCC will also receive a $75,000 tax credit in the first quarter 2015;

and it is further RESOLVED 2. The Properties inclusive of Lots 1 and 1.01 in Block 174 shall be assessed for tax year 2011 at a combined total value of $22 million to be allocated and directed by West Orange Tax Assessor 1; 3. CCC agrees not to file any further farmland assessment applications for the Properties through 201 5; 4. CCC agrees not to file or prosecute any valuation appeals on the Properties for the years 2011 through 2015 provided the total assessment does not exceed $22 million. To the extent that there is any increase in assessment for the Properties, CCC reserves all rights. 5. In the event of any conveyance between now and 2015, CCC agrees that any new owner shall be bound by this agreement and shall not seek to reduce the $22 million assessment and shall not seek any farmland assessments for the P roperties through 2015. 1 To the extent that the final tax rate has not been struck for 2011, CCC reserves the right to file an appeal for 2011 so as to ensure that the aggregate tax for both lots does not exceed the sum of $660,000. If the combined final 2011 real estate tax for Lots 1 and 1.01 exceed $660,000, the 2011 appeal will be settled upon terms reducing the combined assessment to an amount that will produce a final 2011 tax bill of $660,000. In the event the final 2011 total tax due is $660,000 or less, the 2011 tax appeal will be withdrawn with prejudice. Karen J. Carnevale, Municipal Clerk Sal M. Anderton, Council President Adopted: September 28, 2010

documents.title: Recognizing Hispanic Heritage Month and celebrating the heritage and culture of Latinos in the United States and their immense contributions to the Nation.

pages.text: 248-10 September 28, 2010 RESOLUTION Recognizing Hispanic Heritage Month and celebrating the heritage and culture of Latinos in the United States and their immense contributions to the Nation. Whereas, from September 15, 2010, through October 15, 2010, the United States celebrates Hispanic Heritage Month; Whereas, the Census Bureau estimates the Hispanic population in the United States at almost 47,800,000 people, making Hispanic Americans the largest ethnic minority within the United States; Whereas, 1 in 5 United States public school students is Hispanic, and the total number of Hispanic students enrolled in public schools in the United States is expected to reach 28,000,000 by 2050; Whereas, the purchasing power of Hispanic Americans is nearly $1,000,000,000,000, and there are more than 2,300,000 Hispanic-owned firms in the United States, supporting millions of employees nationwide and greatly contributing to the economic sector, especially retail trade, wholesale trade, food services, and construction; Whereas, Hispanic Americans serve in all branches of the Armed Forces and have bravely fought in every war in the history of the United States; Whereas, more than 28,000 Hispanics currently serve with distinction in Afghanistan and Iraq; Whereas, 140,000 Hispanic soldiers served in the Korean War; Whereas, more than 80,000 Hispanics served in the Vietnam War, representing 5.5 percent of individuals who made the ultimate sacrifice for their country in that conflict although they comprised only 4.5 percent of the United States population at the time; Whereas, as of August 7, 2010, 561 United States military fatalities in Iraq and Afghanistan have been Hispanic; Whereas, as of September 30, 2009, there were approximately 1,332,033 Hispanic veterans of the Armed Forces; Whereas, 41 Hispanic Americans have received the Congressional Medal of Honor, the highest award for valor in action against an enemy force which can be bestowed upon an individual serving in the United States Armed Forces; Whereas, Hispanic Americans are dedicated public servants, holding posts at the highest levels of government, including 1 seat on the Supreme Court, 1 seat in the Senate, 28 seats in the House of Representatives, and 2 seats in the Cabinet; and Whereas, Hispanic Americans harbor a deep commitment to family and community, an enduring work ethic, and a perseverance to succeed and contribute to society: Now, Therefore, B e it Resolved, t hat the Township Council of the Township of West Orange urges the people of the Township to observe Hispanic Heritage Month with appropriate programs and activities that appreciate the cultural contributions of Latinos to American life. Karen J. Carnevale, Municipal Clerk Sal M. Anderton, Council President Adopted: September 28, 2010 PDF text

( ) 1. Discussion of any material, the disclosure of which constitutes an invasion of individual privacy.. ( ) 2. A collective bargaining agreement or the terms of provisions of same. ( ) 3. Techniques or tactic utilized to protect the safety and property of the public provided that their disclosure could impair such protection. ( ) 4. An investigation of violations o r possible violations of the laws of the State of New Jersey and/ or the Township of West Orange Administrative Code. ( X ) 5. 240-10 September 14, 2010 RESOLUTION Whereas, Mitochondria are the power plants in every cell of a person’s body, and create more than 90% of the energy needed by the body to sustain life and support growth; and Whereas, Mitochondria may not function correctly due to genetic defects, damage caused by drugs or by destructive molecules called free radicals; and Whereas, Mitochondrial diseases can cause isolated symptoms like seizures, low blood counts, blindness, deafness, dementia, heart failure and progressive muscle weakness, but more often they cause failure of several organ systems in sequence; and Whereas, It is estimated that more than one in 4,000 children born in the United States each year will develop a mitochondrial disease by ten years of age; and Whereas, Since mitochondrial disorders mimic other diseases, it is believed that they are under diagnosed; and Whereas, Currently, no cure exists, but early diagnosis can help patients and their families use proper medication and nutritional supplements to treat the disorder, improve the quality of life, and even prolong life; and Whereas, Through public awareness, the Township of West Orange seeks to minimize the devastating effects of Mitochondrial diseases among all West Orange citizens, Now, Therefore, Be It Resolved, that the Mayor and the Township Council of the Township of West Orange do hereby recognize September 19 - 25, 20 10 to be, M itochondrial Disease Awareness Week a nd urge all the citizens of the Township of West Orange to take cognizance of this event and participate fittingly in its observance. Karen J. Carnevale, Municipal Clerk Sal M. Anderton, Council President Adopted: September 14, 2010

238-10 September 14, 2010 R E S O L U T I O N WHEREAS, the Township Council on August 11, 2009 awarded a contract entitled “2009 Phase IV Street Improvements – Various Streets” to DLS Contracting, Inc., 633 Franklin Avenue – Suite 170, Nutley, New Jersey 07110 in the amount of $1,579,630.98; and WHEREAS, the award of this contract included the Base Bid, Alternate A, Alternate 1B, Alternate 1C, Alternate 1D and Alternate E; and WHEREAS, Alternate E was for additional work at the unit prices bid for the estimated quantity of additional work; and WHEREAS, the unit prices bid for all the Alternates were the same for the Base Bid; and WHEREAS, during the performance of this contract the contractor performed work as directed which included additional curb and sidewalk, pavement repair and pavement leveling all at the unit prices bid for the Base Bid and Alternates; and WHEREAS, to compensate the contractor for this additional work and allow the contractor to continue with the streets improvements originally specified in the bid documents at the unit prices bid the Township Engineer requests an additional appropriation from the 2009 Capital Budget for Street Resurfacing in the amount of $275,000; and WHEREAS, sufficient funds exist for this work; and WHEREAS, the Township Council concurs in the foregoing. NOW THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED by the Township Council of the Township of West Orange that an additional appropriation of $275,000 be authorized for the contract “2009 Phase IV Street Improvements – Various Streets” with DLS Contracting Inc. of 633 Franklin Avenue, Nutley, New Jersey to continue work in accordance with that contract at the unit prices bid. Karen J. Carnevale, Municipal Clerk Sal M. Anderton, Council President Adopted: September 14, 2010

234-10 September 14, 2010 RESOLUTION WHEREAS, on August 5, 2010 a sanitary sewer backup occurred on Valley Road just east of Kingsley Street due to the collapse of several portions of the Township’s original easterly sanitary interceptor sewer installed about a century ago; and WHEREAS, due to the depth and size of the sewer main its reconstruction was beyond the capabilities of the Public Works Department; and WHEREAS, the reconstruction needed to be performed on an expedited basis to prevent sewage backups into businesses and homes on several streets in the Valley which were jeopardizing public health and welfare; and WHEREAS, the Municipal Engineer contacted the firm of Grabowski Construction, Inc. of 770 Northfield Avenue, West Orange, New Jersey to perform emergency construction; and WHEREAS, Grabowski Construction, Inc. submitted a proposal dated August 9, 2010 to perform the emergency construction for a fee of $110,320 which included police traffic director hours; and WHEREAS, this proposal was acceptable to the Municipal Engineer who authorized the work; and WHEREAS, Grabowski Construction, Inc. performed the construction to the sanitary sewer on August 9 thru August 14, 2010, and they repaired the pavement on August 16 thru August 19, 2010 for a final fee of $136,811.50; and WHEREAS, the final fee included the costs of additional Police Traffic Directors and additional costs for wet excavation and the restoration of the Columbus Island; and WHEREAS, the final cost is acceptable to the Township Engineer. NOW THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED, by the Township Council of the Township of West Orange that an emergency appropriation in the amount of $136,811.0 is authorized to pay

Grabowski Construction, Inc. for emergency sewer construction to the Township’s sanitary sewer main on Valley Road at Kingsley Street. BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that this work was performed pursuant to the provisions of the Local Public Contracts Law, Emergency Contracts N.J.S.A. 40A:11-6 as the work was required to protect public health and welfare. Sal M. Anderton, Council President Karen J. Carnevale, Municipal Clerk Adopted: September 14, 2010

230-10 September 14, 2010 RESOLUTION WHEREAS, the opportunities for citizen leadership have never been greater; and WHEREAS, national studies have shown that voluntary community and public service have been in a steady decline; and WHEREAS, Congress established September 17th as “Citizenship Day;” and WHEREAS, polling data indicates that a significant portion of New Jersey citizens would like to be active in their communities; and WHEREAS, appointments to municipal boards and commissions and local emergency response agencies offer the easiest opportunities for regular citizens with limited time to be able to contribute their leadership; and WHEREAS, the Township of West Orange is determined to be an example to other municipal communities across New Jersey in recruiting and educating its citizens about leadership and service opportunities; and NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED BY THE TOWNSHIP OF WEST ORANGE, COUNTY OF ESSEX, STATE OF NEW JERSEY, hereby establishes and declares that September 17th shall be the Township of West Orange Citizen Service Day and that the following minimum steps be taken to facilitate recruitment and education regarding public service opportunities; and BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, the citizens of the Township of West Orange with personal invitation to new residents, shall be invited to a forum on community service opportunities which shall include, but not be limited to, appointed government board and commission posts and membership in emergency response agencies. The Mayor and one or more members of the Council shall welcome residents to service at this forum; and BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, one or more members of the Township of West Orange government boards and commissions and emergency response agencies whose service has been exemplary shall be honored at the aforementioned Forum; and BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, the Forum shall also include an educational portion on the function and importance of municipal boards and commissions and volunteer emergency response agencies, as well as the process by which citizens may apply to serve. Sal M. Anderton, Council President Karen J. Carnevale, Municipal Clerk Adopted: September 14, 2010

documents.title: ACKNOWLEDGING THE MONTH OF SEPTEMBER AS NATIONAL OVARIAN CANCER MONTH

pages.text: 229-10 September 14, 2010 RESOLUTION ACKNOWLEDGING THE MONTH OF SEPTEMBER AS NATIONAL OVARIAN CANCER MONTH WHEREAS, ovarian cancer is the eighth most common cancer in women and accounts for more deaths than any other cancer of the female reproductive system; and WHEREAS, statistics show that when ovarian cancer is diagnosed early, the chance for a cure is much greater; and WHEREAS, the American Cancer Society estimate d that there w ould be 21,550 new cases of ovarian cancer in 200 9 in the United States and an estimated 14,900 deaths from this disease; and WHEREAS, only 19 percent of ovarian cancers are discovered before they have spread outside the ovaries; and WHEREAS, in the past, ovarian cancer was known as a silent killer, but modern research has shown that perception to be incorrect; and WHEREAS, Women diagnosed with ovarian cancer in 1975 experienced a five -year survival rate of 34.8 percent; today, the American Cancer Society estimates the rate to be 46 percent.; and WHEREAS, the most common symptoms of ovarian cancer have been identified as: (1) Bloating; (2) Pelvic or abdominal pain; (3) Trouble eating or feeling full quickly; and (4) Urinary symptoms, such as urgent or frequent feelings of needing to go; and WHEREAS, medical experts recommend that while these same symptoms are known to occur with many different types of illnesses, if there is an unusual occurrence or frequency of occurrences, or if they last for more than a few weeks, they should prompt a woman to see a doctor, preferably a gynecologist; now, therefore, BE IT RESOLVED that primary health care providers and cancer organizations are urged to develop and implement educational strategies to inform women of the common symptoms of ovarian cancer; NOW, THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED, that the Township Council of the Township of West Orange hereby proclaims the month of September as “ NATIONAL OVARIAN CANCER MONTH ” Sal M. Anderton, Council President Karen J. Carnevale, Municipal Clerk Adopted: September 14, 2010
